reader_question: How much should my salary go up with inflation?
decision_gap: Competing calculators return one adjusted amount; the reader also needs the comparison with today's pay and the raise that matches the latest price change.
method: calculated: adjusted = salary × CPI-U(Sep 2026) ÷ CPI-U(annual average of the year); gap and per-year real change; keep-pace raise = current × 12-month CPI-U change
assumptions: national CPI-U all items, not seasonally adjusted

findings.label: calculated
findings.text: $52,000 in 2010 = $80,350 in September 2026 dollars; a $78,000 salary is $2,350 (2.9%) behind, a real change of about -0.18% a year although pay rose about 2.5% a year.

findings.label: calculated
findings.text: Matching the last 12 months of prices takes a raise of about 3.7% ($2,915 on $78,000).

counterexample: $60,000 in 2020 → $64,000 now: a 6.7% nominal raise is 18.1% behind prices (adjusted $78,113).
would_change: A different index (CPI-W, chained CPI, regional CPI) or a newer CPI month changes the figures slightly.
medium: interactive tool — the reader's two salaries and year change the answer

provenance.scopeAndLimits: national CPI-U; Oct 2025 not published by BLS
provenance.publicMethod: howItWorks section + tool footnote name the BLS series and formula
